title: GTA 6 Sales: Analysts Eye 55 Million Copies by March 2027
description: GTA 6 sales could reach 55 million copies by March 2027, and one analyst expects a blended price near $90, per GameSpot's report on analyst forecasts.

body.text: GTA 6 sales are already being forecast at record-setting levels, days before the game launches on November 19. According to GameSpot, which cites a roundup from Investor's Business Daily, one analyst expects 55 million copies by the end of Take-Two's fiscal 2027 in March 2027. It matters because the numbers show how much of the games industry is riding on a single release.
GTA 6 sales forecasts: what the analysts say

Brian Pitz of BMO Capital Markets says GTA 6 could sell 55 million copies in fiscal 2027. He believes 45 million of those could arrive in the launch quarter alone. That is well above the 34.2 million figure IBD compiled from other estimates.

Raymond James analyst Andrew Marok is slightly more cautious, forecasting 50 million units for the fiscal year. Circana's Mat Piscatella called the launch "an outlier in every respect" and said it is "in its own league" in terms of both investment and anticipation.
GTA 6 arrives with an $80 standard edition and a $100 Ultimate Edition. Marok expects the blended average selling price to land close to $90.
That figure depends on which edition buyers pick. Sensor Tower data suggested early preorders leaned toward the $100 version, but the split could be around 50/50 by launch, according to the report.

Sensor Tower says GTA 6 has already sold 12 million copies and generated $1.2 billion in revenue. For comparison, GTA 5 took 72 hours after release to pass $1 billion. GTA 6 apparently hit that mark a week before launch.
Why investors care about GTA Online

Morgan Stanley's Matthew Cost says strong launch sales could create a "large potential audience" for the next version of GTA Online. He calls that a possible "next major catalyst" for Take-Two's stock. The shares are down about 10% in 2026 and trade around $228.

Rockstar has not announced an online mode for GTA 6. Given how well GTA Online performed for GTA 5, analysts expect one, but that remains unconfirmed. GameSpot notes that any such mode would likely bring microtransactions, which could frustrate players even as it pleases investors.

D.A. Davidson analyst Wyatt Swanson says Take-Two shares could rise to $300. He believes Rockstar will release a PC edition and a "GTA Online 2.0", which he says would "enable structurally higher margins." Rockstar has not confirmed either, so treat it as an analyst's view.

The first real data point is launch week, when actual sales can be compared with the 34.2 million consensus and Pitz's 45 million call. After that, watch for any word from Rockstar on GTA Online and a PC version. Those announcements would show whether the bullish forecasts have more room to grow.

faqs.q: How many copies could GTA 6 sell?
faqs.a: According to GameSpot, citing Investor's Business Daily, BMO Capital Markets' Brian Pitz says GTA 6 could sell 55 million copies in Take-Two's fiscal 2027, which ends on March 31, 2027. Raymond James analyst Andrew Marok forecasts 50 million units for the same year.

faqs.q: What is the GTA 6 release date and price?
faqs.a: GTA 6 launches on November 19, according to GameSpot. The standard edition costs $80 and the Ultimate Edition costs $100.

faqs.q: Will GTA 6 have an online mode?
faqs.a: Rockstar has not said anything about an online mode for GTA 6 yet, per GameSpot. Analysts expect a new version of GTA Online, but that is speculation.
